title: Acceleration
examples: How do I use the formula for acceleration?
What is the difference between acceleration and velocity?

explain.say: Today we will learn about acceleration in physics. Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. Velocity is speed in a specific direction.

items: Velocity: speed in a specific direction

explain.say: The formula for acceleration is change in velocity divided by time. We write this as a equals delta v over t. Delta v means the final velocity minus the initial velocity.
If an object slows down, we call that deceleration. Deceleration is just negative acceleration. It means the change in velocity is in the opposite direction.
The standard unit for acceleration is meters per second squared. We write this as m per second squared. This tells us the change over time.

For example, a car starting from rest to ten meters per second in five seconds. The change in velocity is ten meters per second. So, acceleration is ten divided by five, which is two meters per second squared.

faq.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
faq.a: Speed is how fast something moves. Velocity includes direction, so it is speed with direction. You might also ask about speed vs velocity, or what velocity means.

faq.q: If acceleration is zero, what does that mean?
faq.a: Zero acceleration means the velocity is not changing. This means the object is moving at a constant speed. You could also ask what constant velocity means, or when is acceleration zero.
Yes, acceleration can be negative. A negative value means the object is slowing down or decelerating. You might also ask about negative acceleration, or what deceleration means.

faq.q: What are the units for acceleration?
faq.a: The standard unit is meters per second squared. This means meters divided by seconds, all divided by seconds. You could also ask what the unit is, or how to write the unit.

faq.q: Do I need to use the formula for every problem?
faq.a: No, sometimes you can tell it without the formula. If an object is moving at a constant speed, its acceleration is zero. You might also ask if I can just guess, or what if it's not constant?

facts: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
The formula used is a equals (final velocity minus initial velocity) divided by time.
The standard unit for acceleration is meters per second squared.

quiz.say: A runner goes from zero to six meters per second in three seconds. What is the acceleration?
quiz.why: The change in velocity is six meters per second. Dividing that by three seconds gives two meters per second squared.

wrong.1: You multiplied the velocities together instead of subtracting them.
wrong.2: You forgot to divide by the time taken.
wrong.3: You divided the final velocity by the time squared.

quiz.say: A car moving at ten meters per second slows to two meters per second over five seconds. What is its acceleration?
quiz.why: The change in velocity is negative eight meters per second. Dividing that by five seconds gives negative one point six meters per second squared.

wrong.0: You only calculated the magnitude of the change in velocity.
wrong.1: You subtracted the final velocity from the initial velocity.
wrong.2: You incorrectly added the velocities together.

quiz.say: If an object moves at a constant velocity of twelve meters per second, what is its acceleration?
quiz.why: Since the velocity is not changing, the change in velocity is zero. Zero divided by any time is zero.

wrong.0: You thought division by time was impossible.
wrong.2: You used the constant velocity as the acceleration.
wrong.3: You forgot to account for the change in velocity.
